title: Inverter Fault Codes & Power Cycling
answer: Most Q.VOLT inverter fault codes clear after a full power cycle: switch off the AC disconnect, wait 60 seconds, then switch off the DC disconnect for another 60 seconds before restoring both (AC first, then DC). If the same code returns within 10 minutes, treat it as hardware-related — log the exact code, the inverter serial number, and a timestamp, then escalate to L2 rather than repeating the cycle.
quick_replies: The fault code came back
What does error code E04 mean?

title: Diagnosing Low Panel Output
answer: Low or zero panel production is usually shading, a tripped rapid shutdown device, or a soiled/damaged panel. Confirm the rapid shutdown switch is engaged, check the Q.OMMAND monitoring portal for per-panel or per-string output, and inspect for debris, shading, or visible micro-cracks on the affected string before scheduling a truck roll. If one specific panel reads consistently near zero while neighbors are normal, suspect a failed panel or a loose MC4 connector rather than shading.
quick_replies: Show me the monitoring portal steps
How do I request an IV curve trace?

title: Monitoring Portal Sign-In & Lockouts
answer: For Q.OMMAND monitoring portal sign-in issues, use 'Forgot password' on the login screen — reset links expire after 30 minutes. If the account shows as locked after 5 failed attempts, it auto-unlocks after 15 minutes, or an admin can unlock it immediately from Admin > Users. If the system itself shows 'offline' rather than the login failing, check the site's Wi-Fi/router first — a router firmware update or SSID change is the most common cause.

How do I add a new user?

title: Filing a Warranty Claim
answer: To file a warranty claim, gather the panel/inverter/battery serial number, proof of installation date, and a description of the defect (photos where possible), then submit through the Installer Portal under Warranty > New Claim. Qcells panels carry a 25-year product and performance warranty; Q.VOLT inverters carry a 12-year standard warranty (extendable to 20 years with product registration); Q.HOME ESS batteries carry a 10-year warranty. Damage from unauthorized third-party work (e.g. pressure-washing) is excluded from workmanship coverage.

What's covered under warranty?

title: Pushing Inverter Firmware Updates
answer: Q.VOLT firmware updates are pushed automatically over the network connection when the unit is online. To force a check, go to the Q.OMMAND portal, select the device, and choose 'Check for updates'. Do not power-cycle the inverter while an update is in progress — if a push appears stuck for more than 30 minutes, it likely means the connection dropped mid-transfer; power cycle once, then re-trigger the push from the portal.

title: Standard Residential Installation Sequence
answer: Standard residential installation follows: site survey -> racking layout per structural plan -> module mounting -> DC wiring and rapid shutdown -> inverter install and AC tie-in -> commissioning checklist in the Installer App -> final walkthrough with the homeowner. The full step-by-step guide includes torque specs, grounding requirements, and the commissioning checklist that must be completed before the system is registered in Q.OMMAND.

Show grounding requirements

title: Rapid Shutdown (RSD) Requirements
answer: NEC 2020/2023 690.12 requires rapid shutdown to bring conductors outside the array boundary to 30V/240VA within 30 seconds, and array-boundary conductors to 80V within 30 seconds, once initiated. Q.VOLT inverters have RSD built in when paired with Qcells-approved module-level shutdown devices. During commissioning, always run the RSD initiation test at the disconnect switch and confirm voltage drops within spec using a meter at the array before signing off — a failed test is almost always a loose transmitter wire at the combiner box or a device that wasn't fully seated behind the module.

title: Q.HOME ESS Installation Safety & Clearances
answer: Q.HOME ESS units require a minimum 3-inch clearance on all sides for ventilation, must be installed on a non-combustible surface or with an approved fire barrier per local fire code, and cannot be installed in a habitable room, garage-adjacent to a vehicle path, or directly beneath egress windows in most jurisdictions — always confirm local AHJ (Authority Having Jurisdiction) rules before final placement. Battery commissioning requires the BMS (Battery Management System) firmware to be at the latest version before first charge cycle.

title: Permit & Inspection Documentation Checklist
answer: Standard permit packages need: the structural/electrical plan set, equipment spec sheets (panel, inverter, and battery if applicable), a single-line diagram, and the rapid shutdown compliance note. After passing inspection, submit the interconnection agreement and inspection sign-off to the utility — most utilities issue Permission to Operate (PTO) within 5-15 business days, though this varies by jurisdiction. Keep a copy of the commissioning report; it's required for warranty claims later.

title: Q.VOLT Inverter Error Code Reference
answer: Quick reference for common Q.VOLT codes: E01/E02 = internal communication fault (power cycle first); E03 = Grid Fault, utility voltage/frequency outside anti-islanding threshold (verify with utility before adjusting settings — requires L2 access); E04 = DC Arc Fault Detected, de-energize and inspect DC wiring for damage (rodent damage is a common cause) before re-energizing; E05 = Isolation Fault, usually moisture ingress in a connector; E06 = Overtemperature, check ventilation clearance around the unit.

title: Grounding & Bonding Requirements
answer: Every module frame must be bonded to the racking system using listed bonding hardware (WEEB or equivalent), with a continuous equipment grounding conductor run back to the inverter's ground bus — do not rely on rail-to-rail bonding alone without a listed splice. Torque bonding hardware to the manufacturer's spec (typically 90-120 in-lbs for standard WEEB washers); under-torqued bonding is one of the most common causes of failed inspections and intermittent ground fault trips.

title: When and How to Escalate to L2
answer: Escalate to L2 when: a fault code persists after a full power cycle, the issue requires changing grid-protection or BMS settings that installers can't access, the case involves a suspected safety hazard (burning smell, visible arcing, damaged wiring), or a warranty claim needs engineering review. Always include the serial number, exact error code and timestamp, and any troubleshooting steps already tried — this is the single biggest factor in how fast L2 can resolve a case.
